{{nihongo|'''Mitsuaki Yoshida'''|吉田 光昭|Yoshida Mitsuaki|born 1939}} was a Japanese [[virologist]] known for identifying the molecular structure of [[Human T-lymphotropic virus 1]] responsible for [[Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma]].<ref>{{Cite journal
| pmid = 6979048
| year = 1982
| last1 = Yoshida
| first1 = M

| volume = 24
| issue = 39
| pages = 5931–7
| doi = 10.1038/sj.onc.1208981
| doi-access = 
}}</ref>

==Life==
Yoshida was born in [[Toyama, Japan]] and received his Ph.D. in 1967 from [[the University of Tokyo]].<ref name="brh">[https://www.brh.co.jp/s_library/j_site/scientistweb/no57/ "ヒトのがんウイルスに挑む" Biography of Mitsuaki Yoshida]{{in lang|ja}}</ref> After his postdoctoral fellowship at [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]], he worked to uncover the relationship between [[oncovirus]] and [[carcinogenesis]] at the Cancer Institute, [[Japanese Foundation for Cancer Research]] from 1975 to 1989.<ref name="brh"/> He was appointed as Professor at the [[Institute of Medical Science (Japan)|Institute of Medical Science]], [[University of Tokyo]] in 1989, where he served as Dean from 1996 to 1998.<ref name="brh"/> After retiring from the University of Tokyo and becoming Professor Emeritus, he was Director at the Tsukuba Research Institute of BANYU Pharmaceutical Co. ([[Merck & Co.]] today) in [[Tsukuba, Ibaraki|Tsukuba]] and Director at the Cancer Chemotherapy Center, [[Japanese Foundation for Cancer Research]].<ref>[http://www.jfcr.or.jp/laboratory/researcher/1875.html 吉田光昭|研究者紹介|がん研究所 Profile of Mitsuaki Yoshida]{{in lang|ja}}</ref>

==Awards==
*1982: Princess Takamatsu Cancer Research Fund Prize<ref name="brh"/>
*1986: [[Asahi Prize]]<ref>[http://www.asahi.com/shimbun/award/asahi/english.html Asahi Prize recipients]</ref>
*1999: [[Tomizo Yoshida|Tomizo Yoshida Award]]<ref>[http://www.tomizo.or.jp/page044.html 第8回 平成11年|8th recipient]{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
*2000: Medal with Purple Ribbon (Japanese Government)<ref name="brh"/>
